1.summary: Peter blesses God for a new birth into a living hope through Jesus' resurrection, an inheritance kept in heaven; trials refine faith like gold; the prophets longed to understand this salvation; so be holy, live in reverent fear as those redeemed by Christ's precious blood, and love one another earnestly.
1.lookfor: Notice the words hope and imperishable, and the call to holiness.

names.name: Peter
names.gloss: The apostle, leader of the Twelve.

names.name: Pontus
names.gloss: A region on the south shore of the Black Sea.

names.name: Galatia
names.gloss: A province in central Asia Minor.

names.name: Cappadocia
names.gloss: A region in eastern Asia Minor.

names.name: Bithynia
names.gloss: A region in northwest Asia Minor.

insights.title: Exiles of the dispersion
insights.body: Peter writes to the elect who are strangers of the dispersion (1:1). Words once used of scattered Jews now describe all believers, who live as resident foreigners in this world.

insights.title: A living hope
insights.body: God has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, to an inheritance that can't perish, spoil or fade, kept in heaven (1:3-4).

insights.title: Gold in the fire
insights.body: Trials test the genuineness of your faith, more precious than gold refined by fire (1:7). Smelters heated gold until impurities rose and could be skimmed off.

insights.title: Without having seen him
insights.body: Without having seen him you love him (1:8). Peter, who did see Jesus, writes to people who never did, as Jesus said: blessed are those who haven't seen and believed.

insights.title: The prophets searched
insights.body: The prophets searched carefully about this salvation, about Christ's sufferings and the glories after, things even angels long to look into (1:10-12).

insights.title: Be holy
insights.body: Be holy, for I am holy (1:16), from Leviticus. God's people take their character from God's character.

insights.title: Precious blood
insights.body: You were redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, like a lamb without blemish (1:18-19). The price shows the value God places on us.

insights.title: A living hope
insights.body: Peter calls hope living, not wishful. What hope keeps you going when life is hard?

2.summary: Peter urges believers to put away malice and crave spiritual milk, to come to Christ the living stone and be built into a spiritual house, a chosen people and royal priesthood; then to live honorably among outsiders, submit to authorities, and for slaves to endure unjust suffering as Christ did.
2.lookfor: Notice the stone passages and the titles of Israel given to the church, and the description of Christ's suffering.

insights.title: Newborn babies
insights.body: Like newborn babies, long for the pure milk of the word, that you may grow (2:2). Not a rebuke for immaturity, as in Hebrews, but a call to hunger.

insights.title: The living stone
insights.body: Peter weaves together three stone texts: the chosen cornerstone laid in Zion, the stone the builders rejected, and the stone of stumbling (2:6-8). Peter's own name means rock.

insights.title: A royal priesthood
insights.body: You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession (2:9), titles God gave Israel at Sinai, now given to Gentile believers too.

insights.title: Not my people
insights.body: Once you were not a people, but now you are God's people (2:10), from Hosea, as Paul also uses it.

insights.title: Good lives among outsiders
insights.body: Keep your conduct good among the Gentiles, so that though they slander you, they may see your good works and glorify God (2:12). Christians were accused of being antisocial and immoral; their lives were the answer.

insights.title: Honor the king
insights.body: Honor all people, love the brotherhood, fear God, honor the king (2:17). Written under Nero, it gives the emperor honor, but fear goes to God alone.

insights.title: By his wounds
insights.body: He bore our sins in his body on the tree; by his wounds you were healed (2:24). Peter echoes Isaiah 53 again and again in verses 22 to 25.

insights.title: Following his steps
insights.body: Peter says Christ left an example that we should follow in his steps (2:21). How could you respond to unfair treatment the way Jesus did?

3.summary: Peter instructs wives to win unbelieving husbands by their conduct and inner beauty, husbands to honor their wives as co-heirs, and all to be united and repay evil with blessing; he tells them to be ready to give a reason for their hope with gentleness, and explains that Christ suffered once for sins and was raised, triumphing over spirits, with baptism as a picture of salvation like Noah's ark.
3.lookfor: Notice the call to give a reason for your hope, and the puzzling passage about Noah's time.

names.name: Sarah
names.gloss: Abraham's wife, an example of trust in God.

names.name: Noah
names.gloss: Who built the ark, through which eight people were saved.

insights.title: Without a word
insights.body: Wives with unbelieving husbands may win them without a word, by their conduct (3:1). Roman wives were expected to follow their husband's religion; a believing wife was already taking a bold stand.

insights.title: Hidden beauty
insights.body: Let your adornment be the hidden person of the heart, the imperishable beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit (3:4). Inner beauty doesn't fade.

insights.title: Co-heirs
insights.body: Husbands, live with your wives with understanding, honoring them as co-heirs of the grace of life, so your prayers aren't hindered (3:7). How a man treats his wife affects his relationship with God.

insights.title: Seek peace
insights.body: Peter quotes Psalm 34: whoever would love life must keep his tongue from evil, seek peace and pursue it (3:10-11).

insights.title: A reason for the hope
insights.body: Always be ready to give an answer, an apologia, to anyone who asks a reason for the hope in you, with gentleness and respect (3:15). Apologia was a legal defense, not an apology.

insights.title: Spirits in prison
insights.body: Christ went and preached to the spirits in prison, who disobeyed in Noah's days (3:19-20). One of the hardest passages in the New Testament; many read it as Christ proclaiming victory over rebellious spirits, a theme in Jewish writings about Noah's time.

insights.title: Through water
insights.body: Eight people were saved through water in the ark; baptism now saves you, not by washing dirt but as an appeal to God for a good conscience, through Jesus' resurrection (3:20-21).

insights.title: Ready to answer
insights.body: Peter assumes people will ask about your hope. If someone asked you today why you trust Christ, what would you say?

4.summary: Since Christ suffered in the flesh, believers should arm themselves with the same mind and live for God's will, not for the passions their old friends still pursue; the end is near, so pray, love deeply, show hospitality, use gifts to serve; don't be surprised at fiery trials but rejoice to share Christ's sufferings.
4.lookfor: Notice why old friends are surprised, and Peter's instructions on gifts.

insights.title: They think it strange
insights.body: Former friends are surprised that you no longer join them in the same flood of reckless living, and they speak evil of you (4:4). Pagan festivals, guild dinners and drinking parties were central to social life.

insights.title: Love covers sins
insights.body: Above all, keep your love for one another fervent, for love covers a multitude of sins (4:8), from Proverbs. Love doesn't keep score.

insights.title: Hospitality without grumbling
insights.body: Be hospitable to one another without grumbling (4:9). Travelling believers depended on homes opening to them; it could be costly.

insights.title: Stewards of grace
insights.body: As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace (4:10). The word for varied means many-colored.

insights.title: Don't be surprised
insights.body: Don't be surprised at the fiery trial among you, as if something strange were happening (4:12). Suffering for Christ is expected, and it means sharing in his sufferings.

insights.title: Christian as a charge
insights.body: If anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed (4:16). The name itself could be grounds for punishment; the Roman governor Pliny later wrote of executing people simply for being Christians.

insights.title: Judgment begins at God's house
insights.body: Judgment begins with the household of God (4:17), echoing Ezekiel, where judgment started at the sanctuary. Trials purify God's people first.

insights.title: Using your gift
insights.body: Peter says every believer has received a gift to serve others. What gift has God given you, and whom could it serve this week?

5.summary: Peter, a fellow elder and witness of Christ's sufferings, urges elders to shepherd God's flock willingly and humbly, the young to submit, and all to clothe themselves with humility, cast their anxieties on God, and resist the devil, who prowls like a lion; God will restore them after a little while.
5.lookfor: Notice Peter's humble description of himself, and the lion image.

names.name: Silvanus
names.gloss: Silas, who helped write or carry the letter.

names.name: Babylon
names.gloss: Probably a code name for Rome, the center of worldly power.

names.name: Mark
names.gloss: John Mark, whom Peter calls his son, traditionally the source of Mark's Gospel.

insights.title: A fellow elder
insights.body: Peter calls himself a fellow elder and a witness of Christ's sufferings (5:1), not chief apostle. The man once corrected for pride speaks humbly.

insights.title: Shepherd the flock
insights.body: Shepherd the flock of God among you (5:2). Peter heard the risen Jesus tell him three times to feed his sheep, and now passes on the charge. Christ is the chief Shepherd (5:4).

insights.title: Clothe yourselves
insights.body: Clothe yourselves with humility (5:5). The verb pictures tying on a servant's apron. Peter may remember Jesus tying a towel around himself to wash feet.

insights.title: He cares for you
insights.body: Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you (5:7). Humility (5:6) includes admitting we can't carry everything ourselves.

insights.title: A roaring lion
insights.body: Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour (5:8). In Rome, Christians would soon be thrown to beasts in the arena.

insights.title: After a little while
insights.body: After you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace will himself restore, confirm, strengthen and establish you (5:10). Suffering is brief compared with what God will do.

insights.title: Babylon and Mark
insights.body: She who is in Babylon greets you, and so does Mark my son (5:13). Babylon was a name for Rome in Jewish and Christian writing; Mark, once Paul's dropout, is now with Peter.

insights.title: Cast your cares
insights.body: Peter invites us to throw our anxieties on God. What worry could you hand over to him right now?

intro.who: Peter, apostle of Jesus Christ (1:1), writing through Silvanus (5:12). Some scholars think a later follower wrote it in his name because of its fine Greek; Silvanus's help may explain the style.
intro.when: About AD 62–64, from Babylon (5:13), probably a code name for Rome, shortly before Peter's death under Nero.
intro.why: To believers scattered across Asia Minor, mostly Gentiles, who faced slander and social hostility for their faith. Peter reminds them of their living hope and new identity as God's people, and calls them to holy, good lives and to suffer well, following Christ's example.

outline.title: A living hope, a new people, good lives among outsiders
Households, and suffering for doing good
